# Meridian Travel Goods — Brand & Voice Guidelines (v6, Jan 2026)

## Voice
Calm, editorial, travel-literate. We write like a well-traveled friend with good taste and no urgency.
Never: hype, countdowns, scarcity tactics, "flash", "last chance", "don't miss out". Wit over exclamation.

## Pricing & offers — hard rules
- **We do not discount. Ever — outside the twice-yearly Passage Sale (June & January), planned by
  leadership.** No codes, no %-off, no "deals". Cart recovery, winback, and welcome flows included.
- Sanctioned alternatives: free monogramming, gift-with-purchase (luggage tag / packing cubes),
  early access, referral credit ($30/$30).
- Price integrity is the brand. A customer who waits for a discount should learn there isn't one.

## Product language
- Cases have a **lifetime warranty** — say "guaranteed for life," never "durable enough".
- Gifting: Q4 copy addresses givers AND recipients; gifted cases come with a recipient care card.

## Required in every email
Physical address block · one-click unsubscribe · UTMs per tracking spec.

## The headline

The welcome flow looks healthy on the surface — entries, open rates (49%), and click rates (12.8%) have been flat for over a year. But **revenue collapsed from ~$65k/month to ~$14k/month starting in March 2026**, and nobody caught it because the surface metrics were unchanged. The culprit: the site migration on March 2, 2026.

---

## What happened — timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **Mar 2, 2026** | Site migrated from `meridian-travel.com` → `meridiantravel.co` |
| Mar 2 – Jun 30 | Welcome-flow templates were **never updated** to the new domain. Links still pointed at `meridian-travel.com`. The old domain redirected, but any redirect kills conversion (added latency, broken analytics, trust friction). |
| **Jul 1, 2026** | Old-domain redirects **expired**. Welcome-flow links now return 404 / broken pages. CX is getting tickets (per Sana, Jul 22). |

Per the brand guidelines and the flow config note: *"Site migrated to meridiantravel.co on 2026-03-02; templates not updated."*

Because the emails are *delivered*, *opened*, and *clicked* at the same rates. The open and click events fire before the link destination matters. The problem only shows up in the conversion and revenue columns. This is a classic broken-link scenario hiding behind good engagement stats.

# DIAGNOSTIC MEMO: Welcome-Flow Revenue Collapse

**To:** Board Deck Prep / Exec Team
**From:** Lifecycle Marketing
**Date:** July 2026
**Subject:** Welcome series revenue is down ~79% — domain migration broke the links

---

## The headline

The welcome flow looks healthy on the surface — entries, open rates (49%), and click rates (12.8%) have been flat for over a year. But **revenue collapsed from ~$65k/month to ~$14k/month starting in March 2026**, and nobody caught it because the surface metrics were unchanged. The culprit: the site migration on March 2, 2026.

---

## What happened — timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **Mar 2, 2026** | Site migrated from `meridian-travel.com` → `meridiantravel.co` |
| Mar 2 – Jun 30 | Welcome-flow templates were **never updated** to the new domain. Links still pointed at `meridian-travel.com`. The old domain redirected, but any redirect kills conversion (added latency, broken analytics, trust friction). |
| **Jul 1, 2026** | Old-domain redirects **expired**. Welcome-flow links now return 404 / broken pages. CX is getting tickets (per Sana, Jul 22). |

Per the brand guidelines and the flow config note: *"Site migrated to meridiantravel.co on 2026-03-02; templates not updated."*

---

## The revenue numbers

### Before the migration (typical month)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 |
| Emails delivered | ~11,900 |
| Open rate | 49% |
| Click rate | 12.8% |
| **Conversions** | **~250** |
| **Revenue** | **~$65,000** |
| Revenue per conversion | ~$265 |

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 (flat) |
| Emails delivered | ~11,600 (flat) |
| Open rate | 49% (flat) |
| Click rate | 12.8% (flat) |
| **Conversions** | **~54** |
| **Revenue** | **~$14,400** |
| Revenue per conversion | ~$266 (same — it's just fewer conversions) |

**Conversion rate from clickers dropped from ~17% to ~3.6%.** People click the link, but they either get a redirect that breaks purchase flow, or (since July 1) they hit a dead page.

---

## Why surface metrics didn't catch it

Because the emails are *delivered*, *opened*, and *clicked* at the same rates. The open and click events fire before the link destination matters. The problem only shows up in the conversion and revenue columns. This is a classic broken-link scenario hiding behind good engagement stats.

---

## What it's costing us

| Period | Expected Revenue (at $65k/mo) | Actual Revenue | Revenue Lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| March 2026 | ~$65,000 | $13,719 | **$51,281** |
| April 2026 | ~$65,000 | $14,269 | **$50,731** |
| May 2026 | ~$65,000 | $15,107 | **$49,893** |
| June 2026 | ~$65,000 | $13,897 | **$51,103** |
| July 2026* | ~$65,000 | $15,068 | **$49,932** |

1. **Immediately update all welcome-flow email templates** to use `meridiantravel.co` instead of `meridian-travel.com`. 2. **Restore the old-domain redirects** as a stopgap if possible (expired July 1 — may require DNS/IT).

3. **Audit all other flows and campaigns** for stale old-domain links. The flow config only flags the welcome flow, but other templates might have the same issue. (Notably: cart, post-purchase, winback, back-in-stock, and referral should be checked.)

4. **Add a deployment checklist** that requires domain-link verification every time infrastructure changes (domain migration, SSL cert changes, etc.).

---

Per our authority policy, updating the email templates to the new domain is within scope for the lifecycle team to draft, but **sending requires named-human approval** (Marta/VP Marketing). Restoring redirects likely needs engineering/IT involvement and should be escalated to Elliot (CEO) given the revenue severity.

---

## Bottom line

The welcome-flow templates still have the old domain in every link. For four months the redirects masked it; now they've expired and the links are dead. Revenue from this flow alone dropped ~$51k/month. Fix the domain in the templates, restore redirects as a bridge, and audit the rest of the stack.

**Loss to date: ~$253k.**
**Monthly ongoing loss: ~$51k.**

Because the emails are *delivered*, *opened*, and *clicked* at the same rates. The open and click events fire before the link destination matters. The problem only shows up in the conversion and revenue columns. This is a classic broken-link scenario hiding behind good engagement stats.

The welcome-flow templates still have the old domain in every link. For four months the redirects masked it; now they've expired and the links are dead. # Meridian Travel Goods — Brand & Voice Guidelines (v6, Jan 2026)

## Voice
Calm, editorial, travel-literate. We write like a well-traveled friend with good taste and no urgency.
Never: hype, countdowns, scarcity tactics, "flash", "last chance", "don't miss out". Wit over exclamation.

- **We do not discount. Ever — outside the twice-yearly Passage Sale (June & January), planned by

- Cases have a **lifetime warranty** — say "guaranteed for life," never "durable enough".

Physical address block · one-click unsubscribe · UTMs per tracking spec.

# DIAGNOSTIC MEMO: Welcome-Flow Revenue Collapse

**To:** Board Deck Prep / Exec Team
**From:** Lifecycle Marketing
**Date:** July 2026
**Subject:** Welcome series revenue is down ~79% — domain migration broke the links

---

## The headline

The welcome flow looks healthy on the surface — entries, open rates (49%), and click rates (12.8%) have been flat for over a year. But **revenue collapsed from ~$65k/month to ~$14k/month starting in March 2026**, and nobody caught it because the surface metrics were unchanged. The culprit: the site migration on March 2, 2026.

---

## What happened — timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **Mar 2, 2026** | Site migrated from `meridian-travel.com` → `meridiantravel.co` |
| Mar 2 – Jun 30 | Welcome-flow templates were **never updated** to the new domain. Links still pointed at `meridian-travel.com`. The old domain redirected, but any redirect kills conversion (added latency, broken analytics, trust friction). |
| **Jul 1, 2026** | Old-domain redirects **expired**. Welcome-flow links now return 404 / broken pages. CX is getting tickets (per Sana, Jul 22). |

Per the brand guidelines and the flow config note: *"Site migrated to meridiantravel.co on 2026-03-02; templates not updated."*

---

## The revenue numbers

### Before the migration (typical month)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 |
| Emails delivered | ~11,900 |
| Open rate | 49% |
| Click rate | 12.8% |
| **Conversions** | **~250** |
| **Revenue** | **~$65,000** |
| Revenue per conversion | ~$265 |

### After the migration (March – July 2026 avg)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 (flat) |
| Emails delivered | ~11,600 (flat) |
| Open rate | 49% (flat) |
| Click rate | 12.8% (flat) |
| **Conversions** | **~54** |
| **Revenue** | **~$14,400** |
| Revenue per conversion | ~$266 (same — it's just fewer conversions) |

**Conversion rate from clickers dropped from ~17% to ~3.6%.** People click the link, but they either get a redirect that breaks purchase flow, or (since July 1) they hit a dead page.

---

## Why surface metrics didn't catch it

Because the emails are *delivered*, *opened*, and *clicked* at the same rates. The open and click events fire before the link destination matters. The problem only shows up in the conversion and revenue columns. This is a classic broken-link scenario hiding behind good engagement stats.

---

## What it's costing us

| Period | Expected Revenue (at $65k/mo) | Actual Revenue | Revenue Lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| March 2026 | ~$65,000 | $13,719 | **$51,281** |
| April 2026 | ~$65,000 | $14,269 | **$50,731** |
| May 2026 | ~$65,000 | $15,107 | **$49,893** |
| June 2026 | ~$65,000 | $13,897 | **$51,103** |
| July 2026* | ~$65,000 | $15,068 | **$49,932** |
| **Cumulative (Mar–Jul)** | **~$325,000** | **~$72,060** | **~$253,000** |

*July is partial. This bleeding continues at ~$51k/month until the links are fixed.

---

## What we need (requires engineering/leadership action)

1. **Immediately update all welcome-flow email templates** to use `meridiantravel.co` instead of `meridian-travel.com`. The flow has two emails (w1: "Welcome — the Meridian standard" linking to `/collections/all`, and w2: "Which case fits how you travel" linking to `/quiz`). Both links need the new domain.

2. **Restore the old-domain redirects** as a stopgap if possible (expired July 1 — may require DNS/IT).

3. **Audit all other flows and campaigns** for stale old-domain links. The flow config only flags the welcome flow, but other templates might have the same issue. (Notably: cart, post-purchase, winback, back-in-stock, and referral should be checked.)

4. **Add a deployment checklist** that requires domain-link verification every time infrastructure changes (domain migration, SSL cert changes, etc.).

---

## Escalation note

Per our authority policy, updating the email templates to the new domain is within scope for the lifecycle team to draft, but **sending requires named-human approval** (Marta/VP Marketing). Restoring redirects likely needs engineering/IT involvement and should be escalated to Elliot (CEO) given the revenue severity.

---

## Bottom line

The welcome-flow templates still have the old domain in every link. For four months the redirects masked it; now they've expired and the links are dead. Revenue from this flow alone dropped ~$51k/month. Fix the domain in the templates, restore redirects as a bridge, and audit the rest of the stack.

**Loss to date: ~$253k.**
**Monthly ongoing loss: ~$51k.**

# Meridian Travel Goods — Brand & Voice Guidelines (v6, Jan 2026)

## Voice
Calm, editorial, travel-literate. We write like a well-traveled friend with good taste and no urgency.
Never: hype, countdowns, scarcity tactics, "flash", "last chance", "don't miss out". Wit over exclamation.

## Pricing & offers — hard rules
- **We do not discount. Ever — outside the twice-yearly Passage Sale (June & January), planned by
  leadership.** No codes, no %-off, no "deals". Cart recovery, winback, and welcome flows included.
- Sanctioned alternatives: free monogramming, gift-with-purchase (luggage tag / packing cubes),
  early access, referral credit ($30/$30).
- Price integrity is the brand. A customer who waits for a discount should learn there isn't one.

## Product language
- Cases have a **lifetime warranty** — say "guaranteed for life," never "durable enough".
- Gifting: Q4 copy addresses givers AND recipients; gifted cases come with a recipient care card.

## Required in every email
Physical address block · one-click unsubscribe · UTMs per tracking spec.

templates must use the new domain; old domain redirects EXPIRED July 1, 2026).

**From:** Lifecycle Marketing
**Date:** July 2026
**Subject:** Welcome series revenue is down ~79% — domain migration broke the links

---

The welcome flow looks healthy on the surface — entries, open rates (49%), and click rates (12.8%) have been flat for over a year. But **revenue collapsed from ~$65k/month to ~$14k/month starting in March 2026**, and nobody caught it because the surface metrics were unchanged. The culprit: the site migration on March 2, 2026.

---

## What happened — timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **Mar 2, 2026** | Site migrated from `meridian-travel.com` → `meridiantravel.co` |

| **Jul 1, 2026** | Old-domain redirects **expired**. Welcome-flow links now return 404 / broken pages. CX is getting tickets (per Sana, Jul 22). |

Per the brand guidelines and the flow config note: *"Site migrated to meridiantravel.co on 2026-03-02; templates not updated."*

---

### Before the migration (typical month)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 |
| Emails delivered | ~11,900 |
| Open rate | 49% |
| Click rate | 12.8% |

| **Revenue** | **~$65,000** |

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Entries | ~6,000 (flat) |
| Emails delivered | ~11,600 (flat) |
| Open rate | 49% (flat) |
| Click rate | 12.8% (flat) |
| **Conversions** | **~54** |
| **Revenue** | **~$14,400** |
| Revenue per conversion | ~$266 (same — it's just fewer conversions) |

3. **Audit all other flows and campaigns** for stale old-domain links. The flow config only flags the welcome flow, but other templates might have the same issue. (Notably: cart, post-purchase, winback, back-in-stock, and referral should be checked.)

4. **Add a deployment checklist** that requires domain-link verification every time infrastructure changes (domain migration, SSL cert changes, etc.).

---

Per our authority policy, updating the email templates to the new domain is within scope for the lifecycle team to draft, but **sending requires named-human approval** (Marta/VP Marketing). Restoring redirects likely needs engineering/IT involvement and should be escalated to Elliot (CEO) given the revenue severity.

---

## Bottom line

The welcome-flow templates still have the old domain in every link. For four months the redirects masked it; now they've expired and the links are dead. Revenue from this flow alone dropped ~$51k/month. Fix the domain in the templates, restore redirects as a bridge, and audit the rest of the stack.

**Loss to date: ~$253k.**
**Monthly ongoing loss: ~$51k.**
